reason: I’ll start the outward route by lining the strong arterial wall, as the goal suggests.
expectation: I expect a lined artery whose elastic wall can stretch and spring back with a pulse.

alternatives.reason: The capillaries and nearby cells also have a clear exchange role, but I chose to start with the outward route.

effect: The lined arteries complete the outward-route goal, so I’ll work on exchange next.
reaction: The arrows make the artery’s direction clear.
reason: Putting the tiny vessels near body cells addresses the exchange goal; their thin walls suggest materials can cross between them.
expectation: I expect capillaries beside body cells, showing oxygen and food moving toward the cells and carbon dioxide moving away.

alternatives.reason: Lining the venous wall would start the return route, but I chose to follow the route outward to exchange first.

effect: The capillary bed shows exchange across thin walls while blood cells stay inside. I’ll prepare the return route next.
reaction: The distinction between blood cells and dissolved materials was useful.
reason: The venous wall needs a lining before the return route can be completed; the picture also shows valves will matter.
expectation: I expect a lined vein, probably still needing its one-way valve flaps.

alternatives.reason: Joining arteries to the capillary bed could extend the outward route, but I want to prepare the vein first.

effect: The lined veins point back toward the heart; they still need valves to complete the return-route goal.
reaction: The arrows make the return direction clear.
reason: Adding the flaps should help blood flow one way toward the heart.
expectation: I expect veins with valves that open for forward flow and close against backward flow.

alternatives.reason: Connecting arteries to the capillary bed also advances the route, but I want to finish the veins first.

effect: The valves complete the return route, and the new goal is to join the routes.
reaction: The muscle squeezing the vein makes the valves’ role clearer.
reason: I’ll connect the arteries to the capillary bed, following the outward route toward exchange.
expectation: I expect a connected route from arteries into the capillaries, still needing the veins.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the capillaries to the veins also advances the goal, but I chose to follow the flow from the arteries first.

effect: The arteries now lead into the capillaries, leaving the return side open for the veins.
reaction: The branching picture makes the route easy to follow.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should join the return route to the exchange bed.
expectation: I expect a connected route from arteries through capillaries and back through veins.

effect: The completed network connects arteries, capillaries and veins into a route away from and back toward the heart.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate routes joined into one clear picture.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the capillary bed was most worthwhile: it showed what crosses between blood and body cells and that blood cells stay inside.

leastWorthwhile.text: Lining the vein felt like a fairly predictable preparation, although its arrows made the return direction clear.

surprise.text: The picture of a muscle squeezing a vein made it clearer how the valves help blood move in the right direction.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the vessel parts and their purposes were explained, although the compatible-pair menu guided the choices.

continue.text: I would continue: joining the routes was satisfying, and I’d be curious to see how the heart connects to the network.
